modelDistinctions: The chapter's consistent own two-link example uses uniform slender rods, not the textbook's point masses at link ends; derive COM and rotational energies independently.
The kinetic-energy ellipse has semi-axis lengths sqrt(2E/lambda_i), unlike the source unit-acceleration-to-torque ellipse with semi-axis lengths lambda_i.
Use the actual Cartesian tool-point Jacobian for planar translation; the lower block of a space twist Jacobian is not generally that velocity.
The chosen Christoffel C is essential to the skew claim; C qdot does not uniquely specify C.
Own contact lambda is force of wall on robot, opposite to textbook lambda/Ftip applied by robot against constraint; preserve and explain sign conversion.
Near a task singularity the finite map J M^-1 J^T remains valid but its inverse Lambda is undefined at exact rank loss.
Motor2 mounted on link1 has absolute rotor velocity qdot1+s*N2*qdot2; diagonal reflected inertia is only the explicit remote ground-mounted idealization.

Prescribed inverse-dynamics motion is labeled as such; elbow-release animation is a separately solved force-driven initial-value problem; contact view is explicitly instantaneous unless a trajectory is actually integrated.

Gearing demonstration adds axial rotor inertia only to the original uniform rods. Localized motor/stator mass, translation and transverse rotor inertia are neglected; the source full spatial-inertia treatment accounts for them.

The free-body initial orientation aligns nonzero spatial angular momentum with world+z; changing body spin also changes that chosen orientation. Wrench-mode world/COM and body linear velocities are displayed separately.
